evidence.gaps:
Not found in press, after about 45 searches and fetches (the shared WebSearch budget ran out partway through, so fetching was limited to known URLs):
(1) Firm-level dollar PnL for any year except 2018. LCH net gains are $3.2bn for 2018. Two Sigma is not in the LCH top 20 for 2017, 2019, or 2022-2025, so LCH does not publish its annual net gains for those years.
(2) Full-year 2017 returns for any fund (only Compass Jan-Jul 2017, -4.4%).
(3) 2015 Spectrum return.
(4) 2016 Absolute Return return.
(5) Full-year 2018 returns for Spectrum and Absolute Return Enhanced.
(6) 2019 Absolute Return, ARE and Compass returns.
(7) 2020 ARE return.
(8) Final FY2021 returns (only through November).
(9) Named-fund 2022 returns (only 'largest diversified funds +8-10%').
(10) Full-year 2025 returns for any fund (only ARE ~+13% through Nov), and no 2025 Spectrum or Compass figures.
(11) 2026 flagship returns after March 31 (only the UCITS proxy through June 30, plus qualitative China macro losses in spring 2026).
(12) Headcount for 2015-2018 and 2020-2021 (none found in press).
(13) Year-end AUM for 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2022 and 2023 is approximate or carried forward. The Form ADV, LCH PDF tables, Forbes, Bloomberg, BI, NYT and WSJ pages could not be opened.

My rough synthesis, for the orchestrator, is not sourced. Assumptions: gross PnL ≈ avg AUM × composite net return, grossed up for fees of about 2% management and 25-30% performance ('as high as 30%' per II). Format: year: avg AUM; composite net return; net gains; GROSS PnL with range.
- 2015: ~$29bn; ~+12%; ~$3.5bn net; GROSS ~$5.5bn (3.8-7.5).
- 2016: ~$35bn; ~+6%; ~$2.1bn; GROSS ~$3.6bn (2.5-5).
- 2017: ~$45bn; ~+4%, very uncertain; GROSS ~$3.4bn (1-6).
- 2018: ~$52bn; LCH net $3.2bn; GROSS ~$5.5bn (4.5-6.8).
- 2019: ~$59bn; ~+1.5%; GROSS ~$2.2bn (0.5-4).
- 2020: ~$59bn; ~0% (-3 to +3); GROSS ~$1.5bn (-0.5 to 3.5).
- 2021: ~$61.5bn; ~+3%; GROSS ~$3.7bn (1.2-6.3).
- 2022: ~$60bn; ~+9%; GROSS ~$8.7bn (6-11).
- 2023: ~$60bn; ~+7%; GROSS ~$7bn (4.5-9.5).
- 2024: ~$60bn; ~+11%; GROSS ~$10.4bn (7.5-13).
- 2025: ~$65bn; ~+11%; GROSS ~$11.3bn (7.5-15).
- 2026 YTD to 2026-03-31: ~$70bn; ~+3%; GROSS ~$3.3bn (2-4.5).
- 2026 YTD to 2026-06-30, using the UCITS proxy: GROSS ~$5-8.5bn.
evidence.red_flags:
(1) WRONG ATTRIBUTION: one search summary attributed '$8.2 billion net profits for investors in 2022 per LCH' to Two Sigma. Opening the II 22nd Rich List showed the LCH figures there are for Griffin, Point72 and D.E. Shaw. Forbes also attributes $8.2bn to D.E. Shaw for 2022. Do NOT use $8.2bn for Two Sigma.
(2) CONFLICTING AUM: Wikipedia (Overdeck page) gives $34.21bn for Jan 2015, against $23-24bn from Bloomberg and Markets Media around Oct 2014-Feb 2015. The $34bn is probably regulatory or gross AUM. Separately, FT's '>$50bn' in Oct 2017 against Bloomberg's $41bn in May 2017 is a large jump, so the definitions may differ (leverage, managed accounts). Insider Monkey's $48.66bn '2018' figure is regulatory discretionary AUM for a single adviser entity, not investment capital.
(3) CIRCULAR SOURCING: the 2024 Spectrum +10.9% and ARE +14.3% figures trace to one 'source close to the firm' leak, recycled by Hedgeweek, II and Insider Monkey. The 2023 figures (ARE +12%, Spectrum +8.6%) have two semi-independent origins, BI and Bloomberg, which strengthens them.
(4) Insider Monkey's 2016-2018 fund returns cite no source. They are probably recycled Bloomberg or Forbes numbers but are unverified.
(5) HEADCOUNT CONFLICT: Bloomberg Dec 2025 and twosigma.com say about 1,700. Wikipedia, citing Bloomberg Feb 2026, says c. 2,000. II's March 2023 '>1,500' looks like stale boilerplate given ~1,600 in 2019 and ~2,000 implied before the late-2024 layoffs.
(6) The Hedgeweek Oct 2025 'roughly 10% workforce reduction' is probably the same late-2024 layoff (~200 people) and should not be counted as a second cut.
(7) 13F-based 'returns' and portfolio values (wallstrank's '$138B 13F' for Q2 2026, hedgefollow, the funanc1al '2025 scorecard') are equity-holdings marks, not fund NAV returns or AUM. Ignore them.
(8) 'Two Sigma Diversified' is a Schroder GAIA UCITS fund of about $382m sub-advised by Two Sigma, not a flagship. Use it as a directional proxy only.
(9) The Jian Wu affair: $165m repaid to clients plus a $90m SEC penalty are firm costs, and the client losses (~$165-170m) are small relative to firm PnL.
(10) Two Sigma Ventures (~$2bn) spun out as Deviation Capital in May 2026, and Venn was sold to Insight Partners in Jan 2026. Neither should be in trading AUM or PnL. Headcount figures from 2026 onward may drop those staff.
(11) The 2021 'about +3% for the year' Spectrum figure is from a Dec 21 2021 article, so it is YTD rather than final.
evidence.summary:
The press record gives a patchy but usable series of Two Sigma fund returns and headline AUM. Only one year has a firm-level dollar figure: LCH net gains of $3.2bn for 2018, third among all managers, with $15.2bn cumulative since inception. Two Sigma was not in the LCH top 20 at end-2017, dropped out for end-2019, and has not appeared since. LCH therefore gives no dollar gains for the other years.

Fund returns, mostly from Bloomberg, BI and II via unnamed sources:
- 2015: Compass and Absolute Return both +15% net (Forbes).
- 2016: Compass +10.35%, Spectrum +3% (aggregator, unsourced).
- 2017: Compass -4.4% through July.
- 2018: Compass +14%.
- 2019: Spectrum +1.1%; Risk Premia -0.7% and -2.3%.
- 2020: Spectrum +6.71%, Absolute Return -1.24%, Compass -12.21%, Risk Premia -7.6% and -11.8%.
- 2021 (through November): Spectrum ~+3%, Absolute Return -0.36%, Compass +8.75%, Risk Premia +11.4% and +18.2%.
- 2022: largest diversified funds +8 to 10%.
- 2023: ARE +12%, Spectrum +8.6%, Compass -6%, Compass Enhanced -16%.
- 2024: Spectrum +10.9%, ARE +14.3% (H1 2024: +6.1% and +10.6%).
- 2025: ARE ~+13% through November.
- 2026: Spectrum +3% and Absolute Return +3.7% YTD through 2026-03-31 (Bloomberg, 2026-04-06). A Two Sigma-run UCITS fund was +7.4% YTD through 2026-06-30. China macro losses were reported in spring 2026.

AUM: ~$24bn (early 2015), ~$30.5-32bn (end-2015), ~$39bn (start-2017), $41bn (May 2017), >$50bn (Oct 2017), ~$60bn (2019), $58bn (Oct 2020), $60-63bn (2021), ~$60bn (2022-Jan 2025), >$70bn (Oct-Dec 2025, a record).

Headcount: ~1,600 (2019), >1,500 (early 2023, likely stale), ~2,000 implied before the late-2024 layoff of ~200, ~1,700 (Dec 2025 and twosigma.com in 2026), c.2,000 (Bloomberg Feb 2026 via Wikipedia, conflicting).

Implied gross PnL:
- Weak years (2016, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021): roughly $1.5-4bn.
- Strong years: ~$5.5bn in 2015 and 2018, ~$7-9bn in 2022-2023, ~$10-11bn in 2024-2025.
- Error bars are ±30-60%, wider in early years. Full ranges are in the gaps field.

PnL per head for 2024-2025 is therefore about $5-7m gross per employee. The 2026 YTD cutoff for flagship data is 2026-03-31 (2026-06-30 for the UCITS proxy only).

evidence.gaps:
The shared web-search budget ran out after my first 3 queries (200 searches per turn across all agents). After that I worked only from primary SEC data I could download directly (adviser roster files, IAPD Form ADV PDFs and brochures, the SEC order) and from URLs that earlier search results or Wikipedia's citation list had already surfaced. Several of those (Bloomberg, Forbes, FT, Reuters, CNBC, P&I) were paywalled or blocked. A follow-up run with search budget should look for:

(1) Full-year fund returns for 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018 (fund level), 2022 and 2025. I found none, and these are the biggest drivers of PnL uncertainty. The 2024 figures (Spectrum +10.9%, ARE +14.3%) come only from an unattributed Insider Monkey piece.
(2) Two Sigma returns after March 2026: April to September 2026 YTD. The macro-fund losses in April-May 2026 are known only from a headline.
(3) LCH net-gain figures for any year other than 2018 ($3.2B; $15.2B since inception at end-2018). LCH tables are published as images, and Two Sigma was not named in the 2023 or 2025 article text.
(4) Investment-capital AUM for YE2016, YE2022 and YE2024. The $60B figure is repeated from 2019 to 2025 and is probably stale.
(5) Rating agencies and leveraged finance. Two Sigma has no known public debt. I could not search for ratings or debt deals, so this channel is unexamined, though it is unlikely to exist.
(6) Year-by-year Form ADV gross asset values for the master funds before FY2024, from historical PDFs. IAPD serves only the current filing.
(7) Two Sigma Securities, Two Sigma Ventures and Two Sigma Real Estate economics. They are excluded from PnL by scope.
(8) Two Sigma International Ltd (UK) Companies House accounts, as a cross-check on the employee split. Not retrieved.
evidence.red_flags:
(a) Headcount discontinuities in Form ADV. TSI's Item 5.A jumped from 1,454 (Mar 2022) to 1,965 (Mar 2023), up 35%, then fell from 1,954 (2024) to 1,575 (2025), down 19%. The second move matches outside figures: about 2,000 in Aug 2024 (Hedgeweek) and about 1,700 in Jan 2025 (SEC order). The first could be real hiring or a change in how employees are counted. TSI and TSA share employees, so summing entities may double count by up to about 5%. Wikipedia's 'c. 2,000 (2026)' (citing Bloomberg, Feb 2026) conflicts with the Mar 2026 ADV (1,555 at TSI) and the website (~1,700).

(b) Regulatory AUM is gross and leverage-inflated: $139-233B against press AUM of $52-70B, a 2.1-3.3x ratio. It includes master/feeder and trading-vehicle layering, and the 2026 figure also absorbs TSA's clients. Do not use it as investment capital. The privatefunddata.com aggregator shows a corrupted RAUM history ('$11M' for Mar-Oct 2025, and TSA 'no longer registered' contradicting its own text), so ignore that aggregator.

(c) Circular or stale AUM. '$60 billion' appears in 2019 (II, BI), Jan 2024 (Bloomberg/Hedgeweek), Aug 2024 (Hedgeweek) and Apr 2025 (Insider Monkey). Over that period RAUM rose about 30% and fund-level gross asset values grew, so later uses are probably boilerplate. The $70B figure (Bloomberg, Dec 2025) is seen only via Wikipedia.

(d) The 2024 returns (Spectrum 10.9%, ARE 14.3%) come from Insider Monkey syndicated on Yahoo. They are unattributed, the sentence is ambiguous about which number belongs to which fund, and the year is inferred.

(e) II Dec 2021: Spectrum's '+about 3% for the year' and the other 2021 figures are year-to-date through November, not final.

(f) The rogue-modeler losses are '$170m' in Hedgeweek (Jan 2024) versus about $165M in the SEC order. Use the SEC figure. Wikipedia's Reuters citation date (11 Nov 2025) conflicts with its URL (2025-09-11).

(g) Compass is now tiny (master gross asset value $0.27B at FY2025), so headlines about macro-fund losses (2020, 2023, Apr-May 2026) overstate their firm-wide dollar impact.

(h) Large proprietary capital pays no fees. Strategies Fund LLC alone has a $13.0B gross asset value and is 100% related-person owned; Equity Portfolio LLC is 89% related-person owned. LCH-style net gains may or may not include this capital, so grossing up net figures uniformly would overstate fees.

(i) The 'Two Sigma Spectrum Fund' that search engines return for 2025 is often Meeder's or Challenger's unrelated 'Spectrum Fund'. Avoid these entity traps.
